business.description: Andhra Paper Limited is one of India's largest integrated paper and pulp manufacturers, producing writing, printing, copier papers, and speciality grades across two mills in Rajahmundry and Kadiyam, Andhra Pradesh. The company uses virgin pulp exclusively and serves customers across 25 states and 9 countries.

outlook.statement: Strategic priorities: improving asset utilisation and operational efficiency across both manufacturing units; expanding presence in higher-value product segments; strengthening customer relationships and deepening market position in key segments; maintaining operational discipline and cost competitiveness; continuing to invest in innovation, sustainability, and responsible growth.

Entry into tissue and hygiene segment represents an important strategic milestone; upcoming tissue facility at Rajahmundry will diversify product portfolio, reduce dependence on traditional paper grades and strengthen presence in one of the industry's fastest-growing segments.
In CY26, firm target to expand plantation coverage to 12,000 hectares, further strengthening raw material security.
RJ-3 Machine upgrade of ₹178 Crores in progress with target completion of March 2027.
Tissue Paper project of ₹270 Crores awaiting approval from State Pollution Control Board for commencement.

Global paper demand expected to grow 1-2% in CY26; paperboard demand to continue growth momentum driven by e-commerce, FMCG, pharma and sustainable packaging regulations; specialty paper to remain key growth segment; newsprint to face structural decline.

India's paper demand projected to grow at 4-6% CAGR (FY25-FY27) reaching 25-27 million tonnes by FY27, driven by paperboard and specialty paper; writing & printing paper to grow at 2-3% CAGR supported by NEP and education spending; newsprint to decline due to digitisation.

India's real GDP projected at 6.8-7.2% in FY27 (Economic Survey); RBI projects 6.9% GDP growth; repo rate maintained at 5.25% with neutral stance; manufacturing outlook constructive with PLI schemes attracting ₹2+ lakh crore investment; farm forestry outlook supportive due to policy continuity, MSP and PM-KISAN.

Global pulp and paper market estimated to expand at 3-4% CAGR over medium term, surpassing USD 400 billion by end of decade; Indian paper market valued at ~USD 4.7 billion, projected to grow at 13.4% CAGR through 2032 reaching ~USD 11.3 billion.

India's large education ecosystem continues to support demand for notebooks, notepads, diaries, textbooks, reference books and publishing papers. Corporate, commercial and institutional activity supports demand for journals, annual reports, calendars, envelopes and commercial printing grades.

E-commerce, FMCG, food processing, organised retail and sustainability-led substitution are expected to support demand for paperboard and packaging grades. Regulatory focus on plastic reduction and producer responsibility is likely to strengthen long-term demand for recyclable and paper-based packaging solutions.

Rising hygiene awareness, urbanisation, hospitality growth, healthcare demand and food-service expansion are supporting long-term demand for tissue and hygiene paper products. Andhra Paper's planned entry into this segment through a 100 TPD tissue paper facility is expected to strengthen its presence in a higher-growth category and support portfolio diversification beyond traditional paper grades.

The Company remains committed to operational excellence through continued investments in modernisation, automation, energy efficiency and environmental stewardship. Its integrated manufacturing platform, strong plantation and farm forestry base, diversified product portfolio and strategic investments in specialty and tissue paper segments position Andhra Paper favourably to capitalise on emerging opportunities in the evolving Indian paper industry.
Greenfield Expansion Project to be pursued in phased manner aligned with market recovery, demand visibility and prudent capital allocation; remains integral to long-term growth strategy
Tissue paper project commercial operations slated to commence in Q2 FY 2026-27; commercial stabilisation and ramp-up in phased manner
Phased transition from low-yield seed-origin plantations to high-yield clonal plantations to strengthen raw material security

SAP S/4HANA upgrade from version 1909 to 2025; cloud cost containment via local Document Management System; enterprise wireless modernisation; infrastructure relocation; application interfacing evolution to ICF2 framework

Future R&D plans include KA#3 Size Press Products with OGR from different suppliers, products with increased recovered fibre in furnish composition, DIP final brightness and cleanliness improvement, paper cleanliness improvement by upgradation of approach flow pressure screen, new broke street installation, new godown of 2000m2 for 1500T storage capacity, sub station 7.5MVA transformer installation, ETP underground old cables replacement, KA3 new pump house MCC panel replacement, KA3 refiner 1 replacement, KA3 old rope stretchers replacement with pneumatic, KA3 uni-screen online cleaning showers installation, disc filter installation for fibre recovery, KA3 vacuum pump replacement, new compressor installation for power reduction, KA3 new rope circuit from 6th group to pope reel, KA3 new tail cutter installation at 6th group, OBA optimization & cost reduction, optimization of retention aid chemical, reduction in fibre loss, PCC filler increase for fibre optimisation, and dye trials.

Vision to be the top-performing and most respected paper company in India by embedding ESG principles into core business strategy. Targets include reducing carbon emissions, optimizing energy and water usage, strengthening waste management systems, fostering safe/inclusive/equitable workplace, investing in skill development/health/welfare through CSR, upholding integrity/transparency/accountability, and delivering high-quality products with minimal environmental impact through technological advancement and process automation.

The Company falls under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) which is jointly overseen by the Ministry of Power (MoP) and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) with 2 year targets (2025-26 & 2026-27) which is currently underway.

Through these concerted efforts, your Company reaffirms its commitment to sustainable operations and continuous improvement in energy efficiency, aligning with the overarching goals of the CCTS program and our broader environmental stewardship.

The Company has undertaken various modernization and capacity enhancement initiatives aimed at improving operational efficiency, productivity and sustainability. Implementation of the Tissue Machine Project, a significant strategic initiative intended to diversify the Company's product portfolio, expand market opportunities and create long-term value for stakeholders.
